### Key Things to Keep in Mind:

- **Time Limits in South Australia:** For public liability claims, you generally must provide formal notice of the claim to the occupier/owner within **6 months** of the injury, and court proceedings must typically commence within **3 years**.[[1]](https://www.mkflawyers.com.au/service/public-liability-claims)[[2]](https://www.shine.com.au/service/public-liability-claims-adelaide)
- **No Win, No Fee:** Most reputable personal injury firms offer this structure, meaning you don't pay legal fees unless your case is successful, but make sure to read the fine print regarding out-of-pocket (disbursement) costs.[[1]](https://www.shine.com.au/service/public-liability-claims-adelaide)[[2]](https://johnstonwithers.com.au/what-we-do/personal-injury-lawyers/public-liability-lawyers)[[3]](https://www.mkflawyers.com.au/service/public-liability-claims)
- **Gather Evidence:** If you haven't already, try to secure photos of the hazard, incident reports filed with the shopping centre management, witness details, and any medical records from visiting a doctor or hospital.

To help narrow down the best fit, could you tell me:

- **How severe** the injuries are
- Whether you have already **reported the incident** to the shopping centre management or received an **incident report**
